blocks.text: Machine learning is used in many areas of modern life, including healthcare, business, education and daily life (Fig 6.5). It helps organisations analyse large amounts of data quickly; many systems work automatically from learned patterns, which reduces human effort and saves time.

blocks.caption: Uses of machine learning
rows: Analysing medical data for detection and diagnosis: finding cancerous cells in medical images, spotting early signs of Alzheimer's disease or dementia, helping diagnose heart disease, so doctors can plan earlier and better treatment
Understanding customer behaviour; predicting sales and market trends; managing stock; detecting fraud; chatbots for customer service; suggesting products; more effective, data-driven marketing
Tracking students' performance to help improve grades; personalised learning content; smarter attendance and assessment systems
Face recognition on phones; voice assistants; personalised social-media feeds; spam filters; route suggestions in navigation apps; video and music recommendations; smart devices

blocks.alt: A central circle labelled machine learning is joined to four boxes: Healthcare (medical diagnosis, predicting risk, drug discovery), Business (customer insights, fraud detection, sales forecasting), Education (adaptive learning, student assessment, tutoring systems) and Daily life (virtual assistants, recommendations, smart homes).
blocks.caption: Applications of machine learning (original diagram after Fig 6.5).
blocks.long_description: The same few ideas, classifying, predicting and recommending, appear in every area; only the data changes.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Using a simple dataset such as students' marks and grades, decide which part of the data could be used for training and which for testing.

blocks.prompt: Give one machine-learning use in Pakistan's daily life and say whether it is mainly classification, prediction or recommendation.
blocks.explanation: For example, a ride-hailing app estimating the fare and arrival time is prediction; a phone's spam-call warning is classification; a video app suggesting dramas is recommendation. (Other reasonable examples are acceptable.)

items: Healthcare: detection and diagnosis from medical data.
Business: customers, sales, fraud, chatbots, recommendations.
Education: performance tracking, personalised learning; daily life: face unlock, assistants, spam filters, navigation.
